items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: So I said, 'Don't worry about it. We're going to play what we want. But I got a point to make and we're going to play a couple of his tunes. That's all he's going to play.' ... So we went and rehearsed these two tunes for him. ... I said, 'Okay, 'Dud' -- I used to called him 'Dud' -- I said, 'You're

ctx.x: I had -- Those were the two most important ones I had. I had a good drummer. Oh, the drummer, he works with -- oh, God -- Ray Charles, I think. Ray Charles. He's working with Ray Charles. I can't think of his name.

And I asked Ory what could he play and he said he could play "Muskrat Ramble" and "Ory's Creole Trombone". I said, "Yeah." So the guys in the band said, "What do you want that old man in the band for? He can't play nothing." I said, "Well, he's going to play in my band." So I said, "Don't worry about it. We're going to play what we want. But I got a point to make and we're going to play a couple of his tunes. That's all he's going to play."
